description: Ronit (lead) + Anshul — building 'The 34% Question': an atmosphere-coverage checker for spacecraft fire safety. Using NASA PSI microgravity combustion data (BASS-II, FLEX, Saffire), it shows whether a cabin material was actually tested at ISS (21%), Orion (26.5%) or lunar-base (34% O2) atmospheres — TESTED, GAP or NEAREST TEST — so engineers know what to test first.
summary: An interactive 3D fire lab that answers one question with NASA test data: was a material ever tested in the air a lunar base will breathe? Pick a material and atmosphere; live verdicts cite the nearest real PSI test by DOI.
details: An interactive 3D fire lab that answers one question with NASA's own test data: was a material ever actually tested in the air a lunar base will breathe? Pick a material and an atmosphere — ISS (21% O2), Orion (26.5%), or lunar-base Exploration (34% O2 @ 8.2 psi) — and the app shows whether that condition was TESTED in microgravity, a PARTIAL match, or a GAP no test ever covered. Every verdict is computed live from 2,012 cleaned rows of NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion data and cites the nearest real test by DOI. The headline finding is a solids gap: no solid material in PSI's archived flight investigations was ever tested above 22.2% O2, while a lunar base flies at 34% — SIBAL fabric at Exploration shows GAP 11.9 O2 points. The closest flight tests beyond PSI reach further — SAFFIRE-VI burned SIBAL at 31.0% O2 and PMMA at 30.3%, while Nomex at 31.9% did not ignite — but the exact lunar point, 34% O2 at 8.2 psi across a full material set, is still untested. The app includes a printable mission brief ranking all 34 materials by coverage for each atmosphere, and an Evidence view showing the 997-point scatter of every tested condition plus the exact PSI rows behind any verdict. The flame shown is illustrative; safety verdicts come only from real PSI test data. Use of Synthetic Intelligence (SI) disclosure: Coding assistance: the app and backend were written with Muse (Meta's AI coding assistant). All data handling, verdict math, and interpretation are the team's own analysis of the PSI dataset; every number is computed from real PSI rows and unit-tested against known values. Demo video narration: AI-generated voice (Fish Audio, s2.1-pro-free model, "CarbonProof" voice) reading a team-written 76-word script. 3D models: real human-made Sketchfab models under CC-BY / CC-BY-NC-SA licences (credited in the app) — not AI-generated. The flame visualization is illustrative. No AI was used to produce, alter, or interpolate test data, and no verdict is an AI generation: verdicts are coverage lookups against the real PSI dataset.
dataRefs: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) — Combustion Science investigations
BASS-II — NASA-TM-202110011385 (Burning and Suppression of Solids – II: SIBAL, Nomex and PMMA microgravity flame tests)
